description: Classical color harmony systems formalized as angle operations in HSL hue space
base_hue_variable: θ (theta) — the primary hue angle in degrees [0, 360)

harmonies.name: Monochromatic
harmonies.description: Single hue, multiple values. Unified and serene.
harmonies.math: All colors share H. Vary S in [0.3, 1.0] and L in [0.2, 0.8].
harmonies.generative_tip: Map a 1D parameter t → S and L via sine functions for smooth variation.

harmonies.name: Complementary
harmonies.description: Two hues opposite on the wheel. Maximum contrast. Can vibrate visually at equal weight.
harmonies.generative_tip: Use one color at 70% area, complement at 30% for balance.

harmonies.name: Split Complementary
harmonies.description: Primary + two colors adjacent to its complement. High contrast, less tension than direct complementary.

harmonies.name: Triadic
harmonies.description: Three equally spaced hues. Vibrant and balanced. The primary color triad (red/yellow/blue) is triadic.
harmonies.math: Δhue = 120°. Equilateral triangle on the wheel.
harmonies.generative_tip: Rotate θ slowly over time for animated palette cycling.

harmonies.name: Square / Tetradic
harmonies.description: Four equally spaced hues. Rich and complex. Hard to balance — vary saturation/lightness heavily.

harmonies.name: Rectangular / Double Complementary
harmonies.description: Two complementary pairs. Rectangle on the wheel.

harmonies.name: Analogous
harmonies.description: Neighboring hues. Natural, harmonious, found in nature. Low tension.
harmonies.generative_tip: Use analogous for background/ambient color fields, then punch with a complementary accent.

harmonies.name: Analogous Wide
harmonies.description: Five neighboring hues. More variation, still cohesive.

generative_extensions.description: Beyond classical harmonies — variations for generative art

variants.name: Golden Angle Harmony
variants.description: Successive hues separated by the golden angle (≈137.508°). Generates maximally spread, non-repeating hue sequences. Used in phyllotaxis. Never clusters, never repeats for finite n.

variants.name: Fibonacci Harmony
variants.description: Hue positions at Fibonacci ratio intervals. Converges toward golden angle harmony.

variants.name: Prime Gap Harmony
variants.description: Hue jumps determined by gaps between consecutive primes. Irregular but non-random.
